analysis: What changed vs the 6:00 AM brief: the selloff did not fade at the open — it confirmed. Alphabet deepened from ~11% premarket to ~12% early, Microsoft flipped from +1.5% premarket to slightly negative, and all three indexes opened lower (Nasdaq -1.32% leading), whereas premarket futures had the Dow only modestly lower. The ECB hold landed as expected at 6:15 AM PT with minimal knee-jerk reaction, but Lagarde's announced Feb 2027 departure is genuinely new information for the medium-term policy path. DoorDash faded from +5-7% premarket to +nearly 2% — the deal is still being rewarded, just less enthusiastically once the tape turned. Signal: the market is grading on cash conversion, guidance, and segment detail — Alphabet's cash burn, Caterpillar's held guidance, ServiceNow's miss, Fortinet's product slowdown — not headline beats, and even Microsoft's cash-backed beat could not stay green in this tape. Noise: the Marvell/Lumentum talks remain a single Bloomberg report with no company comment, and the Vance/Iran letter remains a reported overture. Apple (+~1.7%) and Meta (+~1.4%) holding up at the open shows the pressure is concentrated, not indiscriminate.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: A lower open: Dow -0.65%, S&P 500 -0.53%, Nasdaq Composite -1.32% at the open, with the Nasdaq 100 down about 1.4% in early trading — the tech-led selloff from premarket carried straight into the session.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open confirms the premarket move rather than fading it — Alphabet is dragging the Nasdaq while the broader market falls more modestly.

headlines.headline: Alphabet deepens to about 12% lower in early trading (from ~11% premarket), on pace to erase over $400B in market value: Q3 revenue $127.58B vs ~$128.22B expected, search ads $63.35B vs $64.96B expected, -$9.07B free cash flow on $51.4B quarterly capex, with 2027 capex set to rise significantly. Cloud still doubled (+103% to $30.7B).
headlines.why_it_matters: Still the tape's main weight — the cash-burn plus ads-miss combination is now being priced in the regular session, not just premarket.

headlines.headline: Microsoft flips to slightly negative in early trading (down a bit less than 1%), after holding +1.5% premarket on its fiscal Q1 beat (revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, $18.6B free cash flow despite $45.2B capex).
headlines.why_it_matters: The fade is the tell — even the cash-backed winner from last night is being pulled into the Alphabet-led risk-off tape at the open.

headlines.headline: Amazon down more than 4% in early trading ahead of its after-close Q3 report; Intel also reports after the close. MAGS ETF down more than 2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Amazon is being sold ahead of its own numbers on the same AI-capex question that hit Alphabet — tonight's report is the next stock-specific test.

headlines.headline: Chips and software slide together: SOXX semiconductor ETF -4%, memory ETF DRAM -4%, ServiceNow -20%+ after missing Q3 profit estimates, Fortinet -26% despite a beat on slowing product-revenue growth. Marvell -12% on the reported Lumentum deal talks; Lumentum +3%+.
headlines.why_it_matters: The earnings-grading theme now spans chips and software alike — beats are being sold on growth detail, and the Marvell leg is single-source, unconfirmed — treat the deal leg as fragile.

headlines.headline: Caterpillar weighs on the Dow, down about 8% in early trading despite the Q3 beat (revenue $20.7B, adjusted EPS $7.20) — guidance only maintained and construction-industry sales slightly below estimates. Offsetting movers: Eli Lilly +nearly 9%, Merck +more than 5%, Chipotle +6%, eBay +2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Industrials join tech lower while healthcare cushions — the Dow's drop is a Caterpillar story, not a broad blue-chip collapse.

headlines.headline: ECB holds rates unchanged (deposit 2.50%, main refinancing 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%), citing rising energy prices as an upside risk to inflation and a downside risk to growth; knee-jerk market reaction minimal. Separately, ECB President Christine Lagarde announced she will step down on Feb 7, 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hold was expected, so no fresh rate shock — but a leadership change at the ECB adds a medium-term policy question on top of the December-hike pricing.

headlines.headline: Carried macro: Q3 GDP beat at 3.4% annualized (vs ~3.2% expected), headline PCE +0.5% m/m to 3.6% y/y, core PCE +0.3% m/m to 3.1% y/y, all at 8:30 a.m. ET; December Fed-hike odds ~84%. DoorDash +nearly 2% in early trading on the $17B Instacart deal (faded from +5-7% premarket); Instacart/Maplebear down less than 1%. WTI -2.2% to $100.47 on the reported Vance/Iran letter.
headlines.why_it_matters: Stronger growth plus as-expected hot inflation still frames the session — no relief for rate-sensitive tech, and oil's pullback is tied to a reported diplomatic overture, not a confirmed deal.

headlines.headline: Other megacaps at the open diverge: Apple +~1.7% and Meta +~1.4% higher in early-session snapshots, Nvidia -~1.1% and Tesla -~0.2% lower. Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after the close; Nvidia's date is not yet announced.
headlines.why_it_matters: Not a uniform megacap selloff — Apple and Meta holding up shows the pressure is concentrated in Alphabet-led AI-spending names and chips, not every large cap.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. Q3 earnings land before the open Tue Nov 3 (11 a.m. ET call) and the $0.525 Q3 distribution ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. WTI easing to $100.47 still leaves a supportive energy backdrop, with no company-specific catalyst ahead of Nov 3.

Into the rest of the session: whether Alphabet's ~12% drop and Microsoft's flip to negative hold, or dip-buying narrows the Nasdaq's lead decline.
ECB press conference follow-through and Lagarde's Feb 2027 departure — any policy-path signals beyond today's expected hold.
